claims.title: Queue job contents may be readable across the web-to-backend boundary
claims.description: `flow:process:web-application>store:message-queue>enqueue-job` crosses from the web tier to the backend tier and carries business-critical job messages, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If transport protection is absent or ineffective, an attacker able to observe that boundary-crossing channel can intercept job contents. The disclosure can reveal work submitted through `process:web-application` and help target the backend processing path; this is conditional on the unverified transport setting.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:process:web-application>store:message-queue>enqueue-job` is a stated boundary crossing and its transport encryption is unverified. Impact is medium because the flow carries business-critical job messages to `store:message-queue`, although the model does not classify their contents.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and authenticate the queue connection
mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ (preferably mTLS for the service-to-queue connection) on `flow:process:web-application>store:message-queue>enqueue-job` and record the verified `encryption_in_transit` setting.

claims.title: Queue jobs may be readable on the worker-to-queue connection
claims.description: `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:message-queue>consume-job` carries business-critical job messages and has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If the unverified transport control is absent, an attacker with a foothold able to observe the backend-tier channel can intercept jobs as `process:background-worker-process` consumes them. The captured job data can reveal work being processed and support later attacks against the worker or queue; this is conditional, not an assertion that the channel is plaintext.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because encryption on `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:message-queue>consume-job` is unverified and the attacker additionally needs a backend-path observation position. Impact is medium because intercepted messages are tagged business-critical-data.

mitigations.detail: Configure TLS, and mTLS where supported, for `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:message-queue>consume-job`; validate the queue certificate and prevent plaintext fallback.

claims.title: Application and log records may be readable on the worker database connection
claims.description: `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:database>read-write-records` carries application records and log records, while `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If this connection is not actually protected, an attacker able to observe the backend-tier database path can intercept records as the worker reads and writes them. Captured records can reveal operational information and any data placed in application or log records, enabling more targeted access to `store:database`; the finding is conditional on the unverified transport control.

quotes.text: The database is also where we keep the application's log records.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the database-flow encryption state is unknown and interception requires a position on a backend-tier channel. Impact is medium because the flow transfers application and log records to `store:database`, whose classification is unverified.

mitigations.detail: Require certificate-validated TLS for `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:database>read-write-records`, disable plaintext database listeners, and document the resulting `encryption_in_transit` state.
Redact credentials and sensitive record fields before application logs are written to `store:database`.

claims.title: Queue credentials may be intercepted while the web application reads configuration
claims.description: `flow:process:web-application>store:web-application-config>read-configuration` transfers settings and message-queue credentials, but its `encryption_in_transit` value is unknown. If protection is absent or ineffective, an attacker observing this configuration-read channel can intercept the credentials held by `store:web-application-config`. Those credentials can then enable access to the queue path used by `process:web-application`; this remains conditional on verifying the transport setting.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the configuration-flow encryption is unknown and interception requires access to the web-tier path. Impact is high because `store:web-application-config` holds credentials and secrets, including queue credentials, that can unlock downstream queue access.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS with server validation, preferably mTLS, on `flow:process:web-application>store:web-application-config>read-configuration` and prohibit plaintext fallback.
Replace standing queue credentials in configuration with workload-issued, narrowly scoped, rotating credentials.

claims.title: Database credentials may be intercepted while the worker reads configuration
claims.description: `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:worker-config>read-configuration` carries settings and database credentials while `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If that unresolved control is absent, an attacker able to observe the backend-tier configuration channel can intercept credentials from `store:worker-config`. The captured database credentials can be used to reach `store:database` through its read/write path; this is conditional on the unknown transport state.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the transport state is unknown and the attacker needs backend-path visibility. Impact is high because `store:worker-config` holds credentials and secrets for database access, enabling a further read path to `store:database`.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS with mutual authentication on `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:worker-config>read-configuration` and record the verified transport setting.
Use short-lived, workload-bound database credentials rather than reusable secrets stored in the worker configuration.

claims.title: Queue contents may be exposed from an unencrypted storage copy
claims.description: `store:message-queue` holds business-critical job data and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If that unknown resolves to storage without effective encryption, an attacker obtaining a queue volume, backup, snapshot, or operational copy can read retained job messages without using the application access path. The disclosure can expose queued work and data submitted by `process:web-application`; this draft is conditional and does not assert that encryption at rest is absent.

quotes.text: The diagram does not say anything about ... whether anything is encrypted at rest.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unverified `encryption_at_rest` state because a storage copy can be accessed outside the live application path. Impact is medium because `store:message-queue` holds business-critical job messages, though its data classification is unknown.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt queue storage and all operational copies
mitigations.detail: Establish and enforce encryption at rest for `store:message-queue`, including snapshots, backups, replicas, and decommissioned media, with managed keys and restricted export access.

claims.title: Application and log records may be exposed from an unencrypted database copy
claims.description: `store:database` holds application records and application log records, but `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If at-rest protection is not present, an attacker holding a disk image, backup, snapshot, or other storage-layer copy can read those records without authenticating through `process:background-worker-process`. The log records can also reveal operational details that enable more targeted attacks against the application; this is conditional on the unresolved encryption setting.

quotes.text: The database is also where we keep the application's log records.
The diagram does not say anything about ... whether anything is encrypted at rest.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:database` has unverified at-rest encryption and copied storage can bypass the application path. Impact is medium because the store contains application and log records, while its classification is unknown.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the database and its copies at rest
mitigations.detail: Require managed-key encryption for `store:database` and explicitly apply the same protection to backups, snapshots, replicas, exports, and decommissioned media.
Limit access to database copies and redact secrets or sensitive request content before it is written as an application log record.

claims.title: Queue credentials may be exposed from an unencrypted web-application configuration copy
claims.description: `store:web-application-config` holds credentials and secrets, including queue credentials, and its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If storage encryption is absent, a person who obtains a disk, backup, snapshot, or other copy of this configuration store can recover those credentials directly. The recovered secret can enable access to the queue used by `process:web-application`; this finding is conditional on the unverified at-rest control.

quotes.text: Both of those config stores hold the credentials the process needs

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:web-application-config` has unknown encryption at rest and storage copies bypass normal application controls. Impact is high because the store contains credentials and secrets, including queue credentials that can provide further system access.

mitigations.detail: Enforce managed-key encryption at rest for `store:web-application-config` and for every backup, snapshot, and export; restrict key use and copy retrieval.
Use a dedicated secret store with short-lived workload-issued queue credentials and rotate the existing credential if it may have been copied.

claims.title: Database credentials may be exposed from an unencrypted worker configuration copy
claims.description: `store:worker-config` holds credentials and secrets, including database credentials, but its `encryption_at_rest` setting is unknown. If encryption is absent or ineffective, an attacker obtaining a storage-layer copy of the worker configuration can recover database credentials without compromising `process:background-worker-process`. Those credentials can then be used against the database access path; this is conditional on the unverified at-rest control.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:worker-config` has unknown encryption at rest and backup or media access bypasses the worker. Impact is high because database credentials can unlock reads of `store:database` and the config store is tagged credentials and secrets.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the worker configuration store and its copies
mitigations.detail: Use managed-key encryption at rest for `store:worker-config`, backups, snapshots, and exports, with separate authorization for key use and storage-copy retrieval.
Replace persistent database credentials in worker configuration with workload-federated or rotating short-lived credentials.

claims.title: Code running in the worker can read queued job data through the worker's access
claims.description: `process:background-worker-process` consumes jobs through `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:message-queue>consume-job`. An attacker who runs code in that worker or controls its host can use the worker's existing queue access to read job messages. This does not depend on the unresolved at-rest encryption setting: the queue serves data through the worker's authorized live path. The disclosed jobs may reveal work originating from `process:web-application` and allow targeted follow-on attacks against backend processing.

quotes.text: a background worker process picks them up

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because the attacker must first execute in or control the internal `process:background-worker-process`; the queue-flow authentication details are also unverified. Impact is medium because that process reads business-critical job messages from `store:message-queue`.

mitigations.detail: Give `process:background-worker-process` a dedicated, least-privilege queue identity limited to only the required queue and message scope.
Audit consumer identity and alert on read volume or message access patterns inconsistent with normal worker processing.

claims.title: Code running in the worker can read application and log records through its database access
claims.description: `process:background-worker-process` reads and writes `store:database` through `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:database>read-write-records`. An attacker who executes code in the worker can use that existing database path to read application records and log records under the worker's identity. Encryption at rest would not prevent this live authorized-session read. The disclosure can expose application data and operational log detail that helps the attacker target the web application or backend services.

quotes.text: The background worker reads and writes the database.
The database is also where we keep the application's log records.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because exploitation requires code execution in the internal worker, and the database-flow authentication scope is unverified. Impact is medium because the worker's path reads both application records and application log records in `store:database`.

mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated database role limited to the rows, tables, and columns the worker needs; separate log access from application-record access where possible.
Record and alert on database reads by the worker identity that exceed expected job-processing volume or access unexpected tables.

claims.title: Code running in the web application can recover its queue credentials
claims.description: `process:web-application` reads `store:web-application-config` through `flow:process:web-application>store:web-application-config>read-configuration`, and that store holds queue credentials. An attacker who runs code in the internet-facing web application can read the configuration through the application's existing access and recover the queue credential. The recovered credential enables the attacker to reach the queue path independently of the compromised process; encryption at rest does not stop this authorized configuration read.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because `process:web-application` is internet-facing, although exploitation still requires code execution in that process and the configuration-read authentication is unverified. Impact is high because recovery of queue credentials from a store tagged credentials and secrets enables further access to the backend queue.

mitigations.summary: Avoid exposing reusable queue credentials to the web process
mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated secret store and issue short-lived, narrowly scoped queue credentials to `process:web-application` at runtime.
Restrict the web application's configuration identity to the single secret it needs, prevent secret values from entering process diagnostics, and audit secret reads.

claims.title: Code running in the worker can recover its database credentials
claims.description: `process:background-worker-process` reads `store:worker-config` through `flow:process:background-worker-process>store:worker-config>read-configuration`, and the store holds database credentials. An attacker who runs code in the worker can recover those credentials through the worker's legitimate configuration-read access. The credential can then be used to access `store:database` outside the worker process, expanding the disclosure opportunity beyond the initially compromised component.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because the attacker must first execute in the internal worker and the configuration-flow authentication posture is unknown. Impact is high because the worker configuration contains database credentials that can enable further reads of `store:database`.

mitigations.summary: Replace worker-held database secrets with short-lived identity
mitigations.detail: Use workload-federated or rotating short-lived database credentials issued from a dedicated secret system instead of persistent credentials in `store:worker-config`.
Grant `process:background-worker-process` access only to the database credential it requires, prevent secret material from diagnostics, and audit every configuration-secret retrieval.
